name: Card-not-present / payments fraud platforms
topic: Beava's current market position - competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: Two layers of competition in this segment. (a) Generic infrastructure used by the buyer to build a fraud rig in-house: Redis (managed on AWS/GCP/Azure or Valkey-after-the-2025-Ubuntu-26.04-default), Aerospike (PayPal 1M TPS, Barclays sub-100ms p99, Caulis-Redis-to-Aerospike fraud migration delivering 1700-2000 TPS at ~100ms / 500ms p99.9), Tecton-now-Databricks (0.8ms feature retrieval, 100M txn/day reference), Hopsworks, Feast, Chalk, Fennel-now-Databricks, plus stream engines Flink, Materialize (BSL), RisingWave (Apache-2.0), Spark Real-Time Mode (Coinbase moved fraud features off Tecton+Spark microbatch to Spark RTM in 2024-2025, cutting end-to-end from 800ms+ to 100-250ms and feature freshness to 150ms stateless / 250ms stateful, while halving compute cost). (b) Internal feature-engineering platforms shipped by hyperscaler-grade buyers as bespoke infrastructure: Stripe's Shepherd (Chronon-derived, partnership with Airbnb began 2022, 200+ features, 75% ML dev-time reduction, tens of millions of dollars of incremental blocked fraud), Uber Michelangelo Palette (fraud is a first-class workload alongside Eats/Comms), Coinbase real-time risk stack on Tecton+Databricks Spark RTM with a tightly-coupled AI-driven rules engine. Beava competes most directly with the (Redis-or-Valkey-or-Aerospike) + (Flink-or-Materialize) two-box DIY pattern from segment H5, by collapsing it into a single binary.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: The closed-loop CNP fraud-platform incumbents that buyers procure as black boxes (Beava is NOT directly competing with these - it is the feature-substrate layer they are internally built on, and an alternative for buyers building in-house instead of buying a black box). Funding/scale as of 2025-2026: Forter - $3B last valuation (Series F, 2021, $525M total raised; Sacra equity research updated Feb 2026), $103.1M revenue (Oct 2024 per Latka), ~620M shoppers / $1.5T eCommerce protected, 10K customers, the chargeback-guarantee market leader; Sift - $1.84B last valuation, $122M revenue per Latka/CB Insights (one tracker reports $35M in Dec 2025 - figure quality varies), 700+ customers, 1T events/yr / 34k+ sites, #1 on G2 Fall 2025 across Fraud Detection + eCommerce Fraud Protection + RBA, acquired Keyless (Oct 2025) and Chargeback for dispute mgmt, no PE exit yet; Riskified (NYSE:RSKD) - public, $344.6M FY2025 revenue (8% YoY), $26.7M adj-EBITDA (8% margin), first-ever GAAP-profitable quarter Q4 2025 ($5.8M net), $298M cash zero debt, guided $372-384M 2026, ~$856M market cap as of mid-2025 per public filings; Sardine.ai - $70M Series C Feb 2025 (Activant Capital lead, a16z+GV+Moody's+Experian Ventures participation), $660M valuation, $145M total raised, 130% ARR growth, 300+ enterprises across 70 countries; Signifyd - private (Acquired/100% chargeback-guarantee), no 2025-2026 funding event; Kount - owned by Equifax since 2021, not a standalone player; Featurespace - acquired by Visa (closed 2024), rebranded as 'ARIC Risk Hub' powered-by-Visa in 2025, productized as a value-added service; Feedzai - $75M raise Oct 2025 at $2B valuation, $70B+ protected payment volume, framework agreement with ECB to be the central fraud-detection mechanism for the digital euro; Hawk AI - $56M Series C Feb-Apr 2025 (One Peak lead), AML+fraud, EU-IPR-VoP-aligned; Stripe Radar - bundled into Stripe payment processing (see hyperscaler_bundling_threat). Visa-Featurespace and the Equifax-Kount consolidations confirm a 'scheme/bureau is rolling up the fraud-platform layer' trend that is squeezing the independent middle. The market is large and growing - $54.6B-$67B global fraud detection and prevention in 2025 at 17-21% CAGR per Fortune Business Insights/Mordor Intelligence - but it is dominated by liable-vendor incumbents with deep network-effect data moats.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Proprietary across the board. Sift, Forter, Riskified, Sardine, Signifyd, Kount/Equifax, Featurespace/Visa, Feedzai, Hawk AI, Stripe Radar are all closed-source proprietary SaaS. There is no Apache-2.0 / BSL / 'rug-pulled' incumbent in the CNP fraud-platform segment at all - the closed-loop ML+network-effect model is structurally hostile to open source. Beava's Apache-2.0 posture is a wedge for the secondary buyer (the fraud-engineering team building a feature-backend in-house to replace or augment one of these black boxes) but not for the primary buyer (the head-of-fraud procuring a turnkey closed-loop scorer).
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: High and rising. Stripe Radar is now bundled into Stripe payment processing - at the time of writing free standard fraud protection is included with any Stripe account, and Radar for Fraud Teams costs $0.05-$0.07 per screened transaction or $0.02 with standard pricing. Chargeback Protection is a separate 0.4% of eligible transaction volume with a $25K/yr per-merchant reimbursement cap. Stripe Sessions May 2025 launched the Payments Foundation Model (transformer-based, tens-of-billions of transactions, 64% improvement in card-testing detection for large users overnight, detection rate on large-business attacks moving 59% to 97%) plus an LLM-powered Radar Assistant that writes custom rules from natural-language prompts, plus a Radar-for-Platforms tier and ACH/SEPA coverage - all collapsing more of the fraud-team's job into the PSP subscription. Adyen RevenueProtect / Adyen Uplift is similarly bundled with Adyen processing and rolled out 2025-end. Visa's ARIC Risk Hub bundles Featurespace's ABA/ADBN models as a value-added service into the Visa relationship that issuers and acquirers already have. Mastercard parallels exist. The buyer that already runs Stripe / Adyen / Checkout.com / a Visa-issuer relationship can now get a 'good-enough' CNP fraud scorer without a separate procurement. This is the same shape as the X1 hyperscaler-bundling threat to feature stores, intensified by the PSP/scheme having unique network-effect data the buyer cannot reproduce in-house. Beava's Apache-2.0 self-hosted feature backend is a hedge only for buyers whose business demands they NOT route everything through a single PSP (multi-PSP merchants, marketplaces, issuers building their own brand).
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: Heterogeneous and webhook-heavy. Upstream producers in this segment include: merchant checkout webhooks (HTTP push, by far the most common at mid-market merchants and PSPs), PSP auth-stream gRPC, Kafka (issuer-side / large global PSPs / Stripe/Adyen internal), Kinesis (AWS-native shops), mobile-SDK direct push for device fingerprint + behavioural signals (Sardine/Castle/iovation patterns), and CDC streams from Postgres/MySQL for account-mutation events. Sift/Forter/Riskified/Sardine all expose HTTP REST event-ingest APIs as the primary integration (the SDK approach), with Kafka/Kinesis bridges as enterprise tier. Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 + framed-TCP :8081 (JSON/msgpack) push-on-event model is a clean fit for the merchant-webhook and mobile-SDK paths - no Kafka broker hop required - and a friction for tier-1 buyers already standardised on Kafka/Kinesis (a thin connector would be needed, not in v0). Downstream consumers are the ML scorer (XGBoost/LightGBM, increasingly transformer-based sequence models per Stripe Payments Foundation Model and Coinbase sequence-features) and the rules engine (regulator-mandated decline patterns + hard velocity caps), both pulling features via batch_get inside the ~100ms auth flow.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Production fraud rigs in this segment run (a) a rules engine for hard velocity caps, regulator-mandated decline patterns, and SCA-exemption decision logic (PSD2/PSD3 TRA), and (b) an ML scorer (XGBoost/LightGBM dominant 2024-2025, transformer-based sequence models emerging at large PSPs - Stripe's Payments Foundation Model and Coinbase's sequence-feature ML are the public exemplars). Beava sits below both as the feature substrate. The buyer typically also runs a third loop - a model-features computation layer (Stripe's Shepherd/Chronon-derived, Uber's Palette, Tecton/Coinbase) - which is exactly the layer beava replaces in the build-it-yourself path. Note that Stripe Radar's LLM-powered Radar Assistant launched at Sessions 2025 is shifting some of the rules-authoring work toward natural-language prompts; this does not change the feature-substrate layer beava plays in.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: Five concrete reasons a buyer in this segment - specifically the fraud-engineering team at a merchant, marketplace, PSP, or issuer building in-house instead of (or alongside) a Sift/Forter/Riskified/Sardine deployment - would pick beava over the alternatives: (1) Single binary collapses the (Kafka+Flink+Redis+feature-store ETL) stack from segment H5 into one process; the comparable in-house references (Stripe Shepherd, Uber Palette, Coinbase Tecton+Spark-RTM, Caulis Redis-to-Aerospike) all required a multi-team multi-year build of a similarly-shaped substrate. (2) ~60 first-class aggregation primitives covering counters, velocities, distances, rates, and distributions - the exact features fraud teams hand-code as Redis Lua scripts or Flink streaming aggregations today. (3) Sub-millisecond TCP batch_get fits inside the ~100ms auth budget Stripe Radar documents publicly with margin to spare and at parity with Aerospike fraud-prevention benchmarks (Caulis ~100ms avg, 500ms p99.9 at 1700-2000 TPS post-migration). (4) Push-on-event HTTP/JSON + framed-TCP ingestion avoids the Kafka-broker requirement that Tecton / Feast / Hopsworks / Fennel and most stream-processor patterns assume - the typical merchant or smaller PSP charge stream is already an HTTP webhook, so the impedance match is exact. (5) Apache-2.0 with no open-core split and no acquisition risk - the only Apache-2.0 player in a segment dominated by proprietary closed-loop SaaS where every viable adjacent OSS has been acquired (Featureform-to-Redis Oct 2025, Fennel-to-Databricks Apr 2025, Tecton-to-Databricks Aug 2025, Featurespace-to-Visa 2024). For procurement-conscious buyers and for issuers/banks/marketplaces who need to avoid the PSP-network lock-in implicit in Stripe Radar / Adyen Uplift / Visa ARIC Risk Hub, the license is a real wedge.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Concrete gaps blocking production CNP fraud deployments today (derived from use case 1a's open_engineering_gaps and SOURCE-OF-TRUTH.md v0 invariants): (1) No TLS and no auth on :8080/:8081/:8090 in v0 - for a PSP or issuer this is a non-starter even on a private subnet; auditors will block it before any production traffic flows. (2) No in-process sharding - a single global PSP's hot state cannot be split across machines; vertical scaling only, ~684k EPS on a single Apple-M4 core, ~100-200 GB hot state ceiling. (3) No cross-region replication - multi-region active-active card programs cannot use beava as the source of truth for velocity state. (4) In-memory only with refuse-on-network-FS posture - all state on local NVMe, node loss requires WAL replay; for the PSD2/PSD3 TRA fraud-rate accounting path and chargeback-liability counters, beava must be paired with a durable downstream sink (Kafka/S3/Postgres-CDC out) which is not in v0. (5) No triggers / no 'fire when counter crosses threshold' - fraud teams want 'when card_hash exceeds 5 declines in 60s, emit an action event to a webhook'; today the buyer must poll. This is one of the strongest pulls for the trigger/action primitive in beava's whole use-case map. (6) No multi-tenancy / no namespace ACLs - a fraud-platform vendor cannot safely host multiple merchant tenants on one beava box. (7) No secondary indexes / no scan API - 'find all card_hashes with >N declines in last 10 min' is not a primary-key get; fraud-ops dashboards and hunter queries need this. (8) No native PII / token-field marking - buyers running a PCI-DSS v4.0.1 audit need explicit posture. (9) No managed/hosted offering - the buyer must operate beava themselves, which excludes mid-market merchants without an SRE/platform team (these buyers default to Stripe Radar bundling). (10) No closed-loop network effect - Sift's 1T events/yr cross-customer signal, Forter's $1.5T transaction network, and Stripe's tens-of-billions of training transactions for the Payments Foundation Model are data assets beava as a single-tenant feature backend cannot reproduce; beava only competes when the buyer's own data volume is sufficient.
beava_position_lens.time_to_credible_offering: 3-6mo for the design-partner shape (one merchant or PSP fraud team building in-house and using beava as the feature substrate), 6-12mo for production-grade at a mid-tier PSP/issuer. The first-tier procurement-non-starter gaps (TLS+auth+namespace ACLs+PCI/PII posture document, items 1+6+8 above) are roughly 1-3 months. The second-tier differentiating gaps (triggers/action primitive item 5, durable downstream sink item 4, scan-API item 7) are another 2-3 months. The tier-1-scale gaps (in-process sharding item 2, cross-region replication item 3) are 6+ months and are blockers only for the largest global PSPs/card networks - not required for the first design partners.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: Strong repo-side signals, zero external proof points. Beava-side: no publicly named users in CNP fraud, no published case study, no conference talks. Repo evidence is unusually strong for this use case: python/beava/demos/fraud/ ships schema.json + events.jsonl with the canonical card_hash/account_id/device_id/ip event shape, crates/beava-bench/configs/fraud-team.json is a tracked workload, crates/beava-bench/src/workloads/fraud.rs and crates/beava-bench/tests/fraud_team_validates_against_agg_op_descriptor.rs confirm 'fraud team' is a first-class internal bench. Competitor-side validation that the segment shape and buyer pain are real: Stripe's Shepherd post (200+ features, 75% ML dev-time reduction); Stripe Sessions 2025 Payments Foundation Model headlines; Coinbase Spark-Real-Time-Mode migration (800ms+ to 100-250ms, halved cost); Tecton's 0.8ms / 100M txn-per-day / 40% false-positive reduction fraud reference (Coinbase, Plaid Signal customers); Caulis Redis-to-Aerospike migration delivering 100ms avg / 500ms p99.9 at 1700-2000 TPS; Aerospike fraud-prevention case studies at PayPal/Barclays/TransUnion/LexisNexis. Buyer recognition is real: build-vs-buy analyses (Unit21, Kount, SEON, Shift, FraudNet) explicitly describe the 2-year build cost and engineer-attention drain that pushes mid-market buyers toward SaaS, but also document the 'over 5 years total cost' inversion that creates the segment of fraud teams who do build in-house. Beava knows who the buyer is - the fraud-engineering team at a merchant/marketplace/PSP/issuer that has outgrown Sift/Forter SaaS or refuses to lock into Stripe Radar / Adyen Uplift bundling - but has zero published proof points to that buyer yet.
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Compete - the feature-backend-for-fraud-teams-building-in-house wedge is real and defensible (Apache-2.0 license posture, ~60 primitives, sub-ms batch_get, no-Kafka push model), but 3-6 months of focused engineering on TLS+auth, triggers/action primitive, durable downstream sink, and a published 'beava + XGBoost in 100ms' notebook against the canonical fraud-detection event stream are required before the first design-partner conversation. Do NOT pitch this as a Sift/Forter/Riskified replacement - that is a different sale, with a different buyer (head-of-fraud, not fraud engineering), a different liability shape (chargeback guarantee), and a closed-loop data network beava cannot match. Pitch it as the open-source single-binary feature backend that a fraud-engineering team uses to build their own scorer when the SaaS pricing model breaks (Sift+Forter per-decision SaaS plus Stripe Radar 0.4% chargeback-protection plus Riskified GMV-based pricing all scale linearly with the buyer's volume, which is the build-in-house trigger).
